# Findings

## Summary
This is an Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield **Connecticut commercial/ACA plan** denial of CPT 27446 (unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty) on medical-necessity grounds. Anthem does **not** review knee arthroplasty medical necessity under its own internally authored medical policy (Anthem's own "SURG.00105 – Bicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty" policy was **archived/transitioned in April 2024**). Instead, Anthem has delegated musculoskeletal joint-surgery prior authorization and medical-necessity review to its vendor, **Carelon Medical Benefits Management, Inc.** (formerly AIM Specialty Health), and Anthem's Connecticut provider communications confirm this arrangement is in effect for the Musculoskeletal (Joint Surgery) Program. The specific governing document is Carelon's **"Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery,"** which contains a dedicated **"Knee Arthroplasty (Total/Partial/Revision Knee Replacement)"** section covering CPT 27446, with its own "Clinical Indications" subsection for Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty (UKA)/Partial Knee Replacement (PKA).

I was able to confirm the identity, title, document ID, effective date, and general clinical framework of this document directly from Carelon's own site, but the tool I used to retrieve web pages truncated the document before reaching the specific numbered UKA/PKA clinical-indications list, so I could not directly quote that specific list verbatim from the current document. I am flagging that clearly below rather than guessing at the exact current wording.
